result:
The proposed answer is incorrect. Its running-bond model does not match the problem.

In this problem, layer n has a = 2ⁿ − 1 identical bricks and layer n+1 has b = 2a + 1 identical bricks. Both layers span the same total width, so brick i of layer n covers [(i−1)/a, i/a]. Brick j of layer n+1 covers [(j−1)/b, j/b].

Two bricks share a side exactly when these intervals overlap in a segment of positive length. That requires (j−1)/b < i/a and j/b > (i−1)/a.

- The first inequality gives j − 1 < 2i + i/a. Since i/a ≤ 1, this is j ≤ 2i + 1.
- The second gives j > 2(i−1) + (i−1)/a. For i = 1 this is j ≥ 1, and for i ≥ 2 it is j ≥ 2i − 1. In both cases j ≥ 2i − 1.

So every brick has exactly 3 neighbors below it, namely j = 2i−1, 2i, 2i+1. A check for layers 2 to 3 gives bricks 1–3, 3–5 and 5–7, which agrees.

Each move therefore has exactly 3 choices. Reaching layer 2026 takes 2025 moves, so the number of sequences is 3²⁰²⁵. The proposed answer, C(2025, 1012), is not equal to this.

VERDICT: REJECT
